tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Shared by tools/clean-setup.sh, tools/spec-setup.sh, tools/auditor-setup.sh and
# tools/porter-setup.sh.
#
#   tools/setup-folder.sh ROLE [DIR]
#
# ROLE is clean, spec, auditor or porter. With a DIR that doesn't exist yet, clones
# this repository into it first (clean: blob-less clone with a sparse checkout
# that leaves out the spec-side folders listed in config/spec-side-folders,
# so their contents never reach the disk; spec, auditor and porter: a full clone). Without DIR, sets up
# this checkout. SETUP_SOURCE (a URL, default this checkout's origin) and
# SETUP_REF (default main) choose what a new folder is cloned from; CI uses
# them to test a pull request's own tree.
#
# A clean folder also gets .git/info/attributes marking those paths -diff,
# so history commands (git log -p, git show) don't print their contents.
# Then it installs config/claude/ROLE.json as .claude/settings.json (a
# byte-for-byte copy), records the role, turns on the commit-msg hook and
# commit template, and prints the session banner.
#
# It never loosens settings: it refuses to replace a .claude/settings.json
# whose deny rules aren't all in the new config.
set -eu

ROLE=${1:-}
DIR=${2:-}
case "$ROLE" in clean|spec|auditor|porter) ;; *) echo "usage: $0 clean|spec|auditor|porter [DIR]" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac

HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
# The spec-side folders, from the one list (since M3).
CLEAN_EXCLUDES=$(grep -v '^#' "$HERE/config/spec-side-folders" | cut -f1 | sed 's|.*|/&/|')
[ -n "$CLEAN_EXCLUDES" ] || { echo "no spec-side folders in config/spec-side-folders" >&2; exit 1; }

if [ -n "$DIR" ] && [ ! -e "$DIR" ]; then
    url=${SETUP_SOURCE:-$(git -C "$HERE" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || echo "file://$HERE")}
    ref=${SETUP_REF:-main}
    if [ "$ROLE" = clean ]; then
        git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout "$url" "$DIR"
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        git -C "$DIR" sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' $(for p in $CLEAN_EXCLUDES; do printf '!%s ' "$p"; done)
        git -C "$DIR" checkout "$ref"
    else
        git clone "$url" "$DIR"
        git -C "$DIR" checkout "$ref"
    fi
    TARGET=$(cd "$DIR" && pwd)
elif [ -n "$DIR" ]; then
    TARGET=$(cd "$DIR" && pwd)
else
    TARGET=$HERE
fi

if [ "$ROLE" = clean ] && git -C "$TARGET" rev-parse --verify -q HEAD >/dev/null; then
    # Apply (or re-apply) the sparse checkout to an existing clean folder.
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    git -C "$TARGET" sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' $(for p in $CLEAN_EXCLUDES; do printf '!%s ' "$p"; done)
fi
if [ "$ROLE" = clean ]; then
    attrs="$(git -C "$TARGET" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)/info/attributes"
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$attrs")"
    for p in $CLEAN_EXCLUDES; do
        line="${p}** -diff"
        grep -qxF "$line" "$attrs" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$attrs"
    done
    for p in $CLEAN_EXCLUDES; do
        if [ -e "$TARGET$p" ]; then
            echo "STOP: $TARGET$p exists in a clean folder. Tell the owner." >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    done
fi

NEW="$TARGET/config/claude/$ROLE.json"
LIVE="$TARGET/.claude/settings.json"
[ -f "$NEW" ] || { echo "missing $NEW" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$TARGET/.claude"

if [ -f "$LIVE" ]; then
    "$(sh "$HERE/tools/find-python.sh")" -I - "$LIVE" "$NEW" <<'EOF'
import json, sys
old = json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get("permissions", {}).get("deny", [])
new = json.load(open(sys.argv[2])).get("permissions", {}).get("deny", [])
dropped = [r for r in old if r not in new]
if dropped:
    print("REFUSED: the new config would drop these deny rules:", file=sys.stderr)
    for r in dropped:
        print("  " + r, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)
EOF
fi
if [ -f "$TARGET/.claude/settings.local.json" ]; then
    echo "NOTE: $TARGET/.claude/settings.local.json exists; check that it allows nothing forbidden:"
    cat "$TARGET/.claude/settings.local.json"
fi

cp "$NEW" "$LIVE"
printf '%s\n' "$ROLE" > "$TARGET/.claude/small-beeps-role"
git -C "$TARGET" config core.hooksPath tools/hooks
git -C "$TARGET" config commit.template .gitmessage

echo "Installed config/claude/$ROLE.json as $LIVE"
CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=$TARGET sh "$TARGET/tools/session-banner.sh" < /dev/null

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Archives a finished session's transcript into sessions/ (R-CLEAN-3).

  archive-session.py TRANSCRIPT.jsonl --role clean|spec [--out sessions/<role>]

Run it at the start of the next session (never on the live session). A
clean session archives only clean sessions; a spec session may archive
either (sessions/README.md). It copies the transcript to
`sessions/<role>/<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl` (the date is
the UTC date of its first entry), along with any subagent transcripts
(`<id>/subagents/*.jsonl` next to it) into `<same name>.subagents/`. It
redacts:
  - tokens and keys (GitHub, Anthropic, AWS, bearer tokens, private keys);
  - e-mail addresses, except no-reply addresses;
  - account and organisation IDs;
  - private paths: home folders become `~`, and per-user temp folders are
    shortened;
  - the local user names seen in those paths and the user running this,
    wherever they appear (ignoring case, even inside other words), and
    `*.local` host names;
  - the local top-level folder (the folder that holds this checkout, unless
    that is just the repository's own name; or --top NAME), anywhere, as
    `<top>`;
  - the owner's private terms (PRIVATE_TERMS, or the gitignored
    tools/[REDACTED:host]; tools/check-private.py), anywhere;
  - in clean transcripts only: the lines of a git summary (a merge's
    diffstat, `create mode` and `delete mode` lines) that name files under
    the spec-side folders (config/spec-side-folders). Each run of such lines
    becomes one note saying how many were removed. A name shortened to
    `.../tail` counts when its tail matches only such files.
It writes `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md` beside the copy, saying what was
redacted and how many times, with the SHA-256 of the original and of the
copy. Every redacted line must still parse as JSON. It refuses to overwrite
an existing archive.
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import getpass
import glob
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

RULES = [
    ("private key", re.compile(r"-----BEGIN[A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----.*?-----END[A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----"),
     "[REDACTED:private-key]"),
    ("GitHub token", re.compile(r"\b(gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,})"),
     "[REDACTED:github-token]"),
    ("Anthropic key", re.compile(r"\bsk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}"), "[REDACTED:anthropic-key]"),

# Session transcripts

Every agent session that works on this repository is kept here as evidence.
A session's transcript is the full record of what it read, searched,
fetched, ran and wrote, so anyone can check that a firmware-side (clean)
session never touched forbidden material (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Clean-room
rules"; R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3).

## Folders, and who archives whom

- `clean/`: firmware-side (clean) sessions.
- `spec/`: spec-side sessions. Their transcripts contain emulator source,
  so `tools/clean-setup.sh` leaves this folder out of clean folders, and the
  clean settings deny reading it.

A **spec** session may archive the previous session of either role. A
**clean** session archives only clean sessions, and never opens, lists or
searches anything under `spec/`. When the previous session was spec side
and the next is clean, the clean session leaves it for the next spec
session to archive.

An **auditor** session (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles") is never archived here:
its transcript holds GPL source, so it goes to the owner's private
repository, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records its ID, SHA-256 and that
repository's commit. `tools/check-transcripts.py` fails on any transcript
outside `clean/` and `spec/`.

## Files

Each role folder holds:

- `<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl`: the session's Claude Code transcript, one JSON
  entry per line, as Claude Code wrote it under `~/.claude/projects/`, with
  secrets and private details redacted. `<date>` is the UTC date of its first
  entry, `<role>` is `clean` or `spec`, and `<id>` is the Claude Code session
  ID.
- `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md`: what was redacted (kind and count), with the
  SHA-256 of the original and of the redacted copy. The owner keeps the
  originals, so a redacted copy can be matched to its original if that is
  ever challenged.
- `<same name>.subagents/`: transcripts of subagents the session started, if
  any.

## How they get here

A session never archives itself, because its transcript is still being
written. The **next** session, before doing anything else, runs:

```sh
python3 tools/archive-session.py ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<id>.jsonl --role <role> \
    --archived-by "<this session's id>"        # writes to sessions/<role>/
python3 tools/check-transcripts.py
```

and commits the result.

## 1. Answers to spec-answers-a1's questions
1. The disassembly line: yes, exactly where you drew it. FM-1-RE documents that quote disassembly in places are allowed on the spec side, facts only; firmware-images/ and anything that is itself a disassembly listing stay forbidden.
2. AirDrop and Mail copies: the app session is checking it on a device. Leave the sentence marked "to confirm (app session)" until its answer arrives.

## 2. The app's answers (record them)
- Package path, confirmed: the app loads a .fwsc through upstream fm1-emu's package reader, the conversion to the flash image and the stock boot, all unchanged from upstream 43ed558. Before the reader, the app refuses a file over 16 MiB, a package under 960 bytes or over 8 MiB, a catalog download whose SHA-256 differs from the catalog's, and M-VAVE versions newer than 015 (by the package's own name), with a message. Around it: a package that crashes the reader is refused as malformed; no patch bank is loaded into the user-patch area (the defaults are filled as upstream does); after boot, the firmware's own saved flash sectors are written over the image, after checks (whole 4 KiB sectors, in range, none repeated). After boot: interpreted CPU, idle skipping, each firmware at its own measured clock. Update HW-93, A1-PLAN and EMULATOR-PARITY from "to confirm" (behaviour only; this is the app's own description, cite it as the owner's relay of the app session's report, 2026-10-27).
- Parity, confirmed with commits on the app's ios-app branch: 0003 b6eced1, 0005 2eab4fc, 0006 e2bbc4e, 0009 a78092f, 0010 67ae970 (rules; timing off by default), 0011 38d767a, 0012 f60b86b. Update EMULATOR-PARITY's table (replace the dated note from #149). The app is now at fwtest 0.7.0's emulator except its own raw-image loader and its Rust rewrite.
- The app's deployment target is now iOS 26 (A12 iPhones dropped; A12 iPads remain), and it picks Low or Normal latency per device by timing a small-beeps build on first launch. Update M9-PLAN's iOS section.

## 3. Clean's questions for the spec side
1. M9-PLAN's build.container wording: update it to the build identity clean now records (the base image's registry digest, and the SHA-256 of tools/Dockerfile and of the toolchain), as RELEASING.md describes.
2. fwtest images that don't rebuild the same: #142's merge pushed a second 0.7.0 image (digest 26102ae9…), not the pinned d7804526…. The harness's determinism requirement says the same inputs give the same image. Find out why the two differ (compare the two images' layers and files; the workflow's logs), fix the cause, and add a CI check that rebuilds the image and compares digests. Don't re-pin anything unless an image is wrong.

## 4. A spec request from a downstream firmware (BR-6)
A firmware built on small-beeps found this: a store with pre- or post-increment write-back whose stored register is the base register itself, as the pinned compiler emits it for pi32v2: `[++r4=748] = r4` (bytes d2 ec 4f 4e; also `[++r1=8] = r1`, d0 ec 1b 10). fwtest stores the updated base; the compiler's code expects the value from before the instruction. A black-box run showed it: with r1 = 0x01C38250, `[++r1=8] = r1` wrote 0x01C38258 at 0x01C38258. Code the compiler emitted this way faulted in fwtest, depending only on register allocation.
- Add it to docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md as SR-10 (from the owner, for a downstream firmware; don't name it).
- Answer it from allowed sources: what the toolchain's own documentation, the compiler's code generation and assembler, and the SDK show about which value is stored. If the chip's behaviour can't be established without a real unit, say so (a Q-n for Phase B), and in that case decide what fwtest should do. Prefer fwtest matching the compiler's expectation if the toolchain shows it intends the old value; otherwise fwtest should fault loudly on the form rather than guess. A patch, a test that fails without it, a new fwtest image and a pin PR, as usual.
- Check whether small-beeps' own firmware contains the form today (the downstream report says it doesn't).

## 5. Notes for the hardware phase (Phase B list only; no code reading now)
Add to M9-PLAN's Phase B section, as candidates to evaluate later:
- M-Flasher: a flasher for the FM-1 and SMK-37, reported to be MIT-licensed, based on the protocol of jl-uboot-tool (a general JieLi flashing tool whose licence we haven't checked). A candidate for the app's later firmware loader (the app side may read it).
- M-Bootloader: reported to be an MIT clean-room bootloader for the FM-1, including the helper M-Flasher loads. A candidate for a hardware package's boot area. It is FM-1 firmware source: the clean side must never read it; the spec side evaluates its licence and provenance first (Phase B), facts only.
Record only what's said here; confirm the licences when Phase B starts.

Finish with "done, ready to clear", Questions, and one merge order.

135:### Spec side and the stock firmware
136-
137-The spec side never opens, fetches or searches M-VAVE's stock firmware
138-files or any disassembly or function database of them (FM-1-RE's
139-`firmware-images/` and disassembly material included). A
140-reverse-engineering document that cites them is not covered: the spec
141-side may read FM-1-RE's documents that quote disassembly in places (its
142-`docs/io/01-boot.md`, for one) and take facts only from them, never
143-code, confirming each with the SDK or another source where it can (as
144-HW-91's `+0x120` is confirmed by the SDK's entry point and linker
145-script). The owner's answer, 2026-10-27, recorded by session
146-spec-answers-a1. The firmware side's limits above stay as they are.
147-
148-### Barriers
149-
150-- **Clean folder.** `tools/clean-setup.sh [DIR]` creates the clean working
151-  folder: a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout that leaves out
152-  `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` and `sessions/spec/` (and marks them
153-  `-diff` for history commands), plus the Claude Code settings in
154-  `config/claude/clean.json`, which deny reading those paths, fetching the
155-  forbidden sites and cloning the forbidden repositories, and turn git's
156-  lazy fetching off. `tools/clean-update.sh` updates a clean folder and
157-  checks nothing excluded arrived; C-CLEAN-FOLDER tests all of this in CI.
158-- **Records in a clean folder.** Each record on the `records` branch also
159-  keeps the harness's own test results and the hashes of their outputs.
160-  Records before SR-1-SR-2 also keep the spec experiments' outputs (memory
its metadata names. They don't prove who made it: the hashes travel in
the same file. Authenticity comes from the signed tag and the
reproducible build: anyone can rebuild the tag and compare `image.sha256`
and the `.fm1img`'s own SHA-256 with `SHA256SUMS` (R-REPRO-4). Signing the
container itself is left for a later major version if it is ever needed.

#### Opening it in one tap (iOS)

What the app declares, so that a `.fm1img` from Files, AirDrop, Mail or a
Safari download opens in it directly:

- An **exported type** (`UTExportedTypeDeclarations`) with the
  identifier `io.github.japes98.fm1img` (the owner's choice, recorded by
  session spec-a1-fwsc): the format is this open project's, under MIT,
  not the app's, so any app or emulator may declare the same identifier.
  Filename extension `fm1img`, conforming to `public.data` only. Not
  `public.zip-archive` or `public.archive`: it isn't one, and Files would
  offer to expand it.
- An **imported type** (`UTImportedTypeDeclarations`) for the stock
  firmware package: identifier `io.github.japes98.fwsc`, filename
  extension `fwsc`, conforming to `public.data`. It is a declaration so
  the app can open such files, not a claim to own the format, which is
  JieLi's update package (section 2). A document type for it with
  `LSHandlerRank` `Alternate`, so the app never takes over another
  app's files (the owner confirmed `Alternate`; recorded by session
  spec-answers-a1).
- A **document type** (`CFBundleDocumentTypes`) for `io.github.japes98.fm1img` with
  `LSHandlerRank` `Owner`, so the app is the default for it.
- `LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace` true (the app's choice, recorded
  by session spec-answers-a1): a file opened from Files stays where it
  is, so opened firmwares don't pile up in the app's own folder next to
  the user's recordings. The app reads it in place, as a security-scoped
  URL, and handles it where it handles an opened URL, running the checks
  above. AirDrop and Mail still hand the app a copy.
- On GitHub the file is served as `application/octet-stream`; the
  extension, not the type, makes iOS hand it to the app.

#### What the release tooling checks

The firmware side's release tool (and its tests) must show: building the
same tag twice gives byte-identical `.fm1img`, `.bin` and `release.json`;

## The build image

The build image holds JieLi's toolchain, whose licence terms are unknown,
so docs/TOOLCHAIN.md keeps it off every registry, and it is never
published. A release records the build's identity instead (the owner's
answer, 2026-10-27, option (b)):

- **The identity** is `config/build-image`'s three lines: the base
  image's registry digest (the Dockerfile's `BASE`), the SHA-256 of
  `tools/Dockerfile`, and the toolchain archive's SHA-256
  (docs/TOOLCHAIN.md; the Dockerfile's `TOOLCHAIN_SHA256`). Together
  they fix what the image holds: the Dockerfile pins the base by digest
  and its packages by a snapshot.debian.org date, and its build checks
  the toolchain against that hash. C-UNIT checks the three are this
  tree's own, so a pull request that changes the Dockerfile changes them
  too.
- **In CI** (the release workflow), `tools/release.sh` reads the identity
  from main's `config/build-image`, checks the tag's `tools/Dockerfile`
  against all three **before it builds** (any mismatch stops the release,
  naming it), then builds the image fresh from that Dockerfile and the
  release in it. `release.json`'s `build.container` records the identity
  as `build-identity:dockerfile-sha256=<64 hex>,toolchain-sha256=<64
  hex>,base=<image>@sha256:<64 hex>`, and `build.toolchain_sha256` the
  toolchain's hash as before. Format 1.0 lets a writer add no field, so
  the identity is in the field's value.
- **By hand** it is a local dry run: the local image `tools/build.sh`
  builds, its ID recorded as `local-dry-run:sha256:<64 hex>`. The script
  prints `DRY RUN`, `tools/release.py verify --publish` refuses such a
  release, and the workflow's publish job attaches only a release whose
  `build.container` is a build identity.

Anyone can rebuild the same image from the tag: `tools/build.sh image`
in an export of it, after checking its Dockerfile's SHA-256 is the
release's `dockerfile-sha256`.

## Checking one (anyone)

From a folder with the release's files:
| `fwtest.version` | string | yes | fwtest's version (`fwtest version`), as `0.7.0`. |
| `fwtest.image` | string | yes | The pinned image: the one line of `config/fwtest-image` at the tag that is not a comment (`ghcr.io/...@sha256:<64 hex>`). |
| `record` | object | yes | The test record of the tag's commit: `records/<git_commit>/` on the `records` branch (R-REC-1, `tools/record.py`). The tag's commit must therefore be on main. |
| `record.tree_sha256` | string | yes | The record's tree hash: the SHA-256 of that record's `SHA256SUMS` file (the hash of every file in it, as "tree hash" means for `vendor/emulator/`), 64 lowercase hex digits. Not the git tree ID that `report.json` holds as `tree`. |
| `record.ci_run` | string | no | The URL of the CI run that made the record. |
| `build` | object | no | How the image was built. |
| `build.toolchain_sha256` | string | no | The pinned toolchain's SHA-256 (docs/TOOLCHAIN.md). |
| `build.container` | string | no | The build container's image digest (R-REPRO-2). |
| `build.ram_used` | integer | no | RAM the image uses (data, bss and stacks), from the build's size report. |
| `store` | object | no | The patch store the image keeps (docs/STORE-FORMAT.md). |
| `store.format_version` | integer | no | The store format's version, so a user knows whether saved patches carry over. |
| `store.offset`, `store.size` | integer | no | Its flash region, a chip offset and a size in bytes. |

unit (Phase B). Each item names where it is
recorded.

  before the USB core's access port that port's "busy" bit; the SDK names
  the same bit as the core's reset. Neither the app nor fwtest models a
  busy bit, and the owner keeps the question open (recorded by session
  spec-a1-fwsc): `harness/upstream/fm1-emu-usb-port.md`, "Left open";
  HARDWARE-SPEC.md HW-86.

  firmware relies on a pair's second half seeing the registers as they

  rotate idioms, including one built with the firmware's flags in a test

  harness test that fails without it (docs/HARNESS.md, "Instructions").

  no behaviour. The app's test for 0007 compares the new address lookup
  with the old one at every address up to the end of the memories and a
  sweep above. For 0008 every way RAM can be written was checked to count
  as a write to code, and a harness test runs RAM code changed by stores,
  with and without the patch. Then the firmware's suite (at `cdfd067`), the
  spec experiments and the harness's own suite were run on fwtest built
  with and without 0007 and 0008: all 284 output files are byte for byte
  the same.
- **0008's own test (session pin-050).** The crate test that came with
  0008 runs RAM code changed by a store with the JIT off and on, but its
  JIT half never ran compiled code: each run entered the block too few

outside `harness/` and `vendor/emulator/` is (CONTRIBUTING.md).

2026-10-22; vendor/emulator/UPSTREAM.md), the same three crates.

| 0007 | 0004 (C) | Peripheral addresses looked up before the memories | speed only | yes (0.4.0) | yes |
| 0008 | 0005 (D) | Code blocks in RAM found current by a count of writes to code, on every build | speed only | yes (0.4.0) | yes |
| 0009 | none | The MIDI output: the UART's transmit side sends bytes at the wire's pace and keeps them with their times, and its pending flag rises when the last has gone (it used to finish at once and send nothing) | model | yes (0.5.0) | no: to apply, with the bytes sent to CoreMIDI (harness/upstream/fm1-emu-midi-out.md) |

content.content:
holds the flash image from offset 0, and the rest of the chip is
  erased; the window shows the app area unscrambled, from flash `0x4000`
  to the flash image's end, and the chip directly beyond it; core 0
  starts at the app's entry (HW-91) with r0 pointing at the boot block.
  The emulator's own package boot also gives the `USR` region (HW-80), if
  the directory names one and it is blank, a default patch bank of its
  own; fwtest leaves it as the package has it. Nothing checks a directory
  head's CRC, a data CRC, the list CRC or the other entries (Q-25, Q-26).
  Unlike the chip, the flash chip holds the app area scrambled, so SPI0
  reads of the area give the scrambled bytes, and bytes a firmware
  programs into the area show through the window as written, not
  decrypted (HW-91). fwtest has `--package` from 0.8.0; until
  `config/fwtest-image` pins 0.8.0, `tools/fwtest` refuses the option.
- Sources: the emulator's package path (vendor/emulator, read for this);
  HARNESS ("Packages"); fwtest's harness tests on test packages made from
  HW-87 to HW-91 alone (harness/tests/).
- Standing: emulator-only (with the harness's own tests)
- Needed by: A1

## Open questions

What isn't known, or is known only from material the spec may not use. A
spec request can turn one into a fact.

- **Q-1. Other RAM on the chip.** Whether the chip has RAM at `0x01F00000`
  and `0x04000000` (HW-7), how much, and whether it can be used. The SDK's
  layout names a cache RAM at `0x01F20000` and an external SDRAM window at
  `0x04000000`.
- **Q-2. Clock set-up on the chip.** Which registers and steps set the PLL
  and system clock on real hardware (fwtest needs none). Since SR-2, the
  clock registers' addresses, the main clock select and the supported rates
  are known (HW-53, HW-54); still open: the PLL's control registers and
  fields (FM-1-RE places the PLL block at `0x00016A00`, which the SDK's
  header names as part of another block; the SDK's own PLL and `SYS_DIV`
  field definitions are switched off), the order of the steps that change
  the system clock safely (the flash and bus clocks with it), and the
  clock when an installed app starts: FM-1-RE says only that the loader
  brings up "clocking sufficient for XIP". Settled by a datasheet or a
  probe on real hardware.
- **Q-3. TIMER0-3 prescaler settings in fwtest.** The SDK gives the chip's
  table (HW-48); fwtest's settings other than 0 and 2 were not measured.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Publishes the fwtest container image (spec side's harness, R-SEP-3) to
# GHCR, for every push to main that changes what goes into it. It builds
# with harness/ci.sh exactly as CI does, pushes it under this repository's
# name with the tag fwtest-<commit>, and prints the digest. A pull request
# then puts that digest in config/fwtest-image; tools/fwtest runs only the
# pinned digest, never a tag.
name: fwtest-image

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "harness/**"
      - "!harness/spec-experiments/**"
      - "vendor/emulator/**"
      - "LICENSE"
      - "NOTICE"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write

concurrency:
  group: fwtest-image
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  publish:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build the image
        run: sh harness/ci.sh image

      - name: Push it and print its digest
        env:
          TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ACTOR: ${{ github.actor }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          repo=$(printf '%s' "ghcr.io/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')
          local_tag=$(sh harness/ci.sh tag)
          remote="$repo:fwtest-$GITHUB_SHA"
          printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | docker login ghcr.io -u "$ACTOR" --password-stdin
          docker tag "$local_tag" "$remote"
          docker push "$remote"
          digest=$(docker inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' "$remote")
          docker logout ghcr.io
          docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --network none "$digest" version
          {
            echo "### fwtest image"
            echo
            echo "Pin this in \`config/fwtest-image\`:"
            echo
            echo '```'
            echo "$digest"
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "digest: $digest"

ENV CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 \
    SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1767225600 \
    RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=/src=. -C debuginfo=0 --cap-lints=allow" \
    LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 \
    TZ=UTC
WORKDIR /src
COPY vendor/emulator vendor/emulator
COPY harness harness
RUN --network=none cd harness && cargo build --release --locked --offline \
 && sha256sum target/release/fwtest

RUN --network=none cd harness && cargo test --release --locked --offline

COPY --from=build /src/harness/target/release/fwtest /usr/local/bin/fwtest

COPY NOTICE /usr/share/doc/fwtest/NOTICE
COPY vendor/emulator/LICENSE /usr/share/doc/fwtest/LICENSE.emulator
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/japes98/small-beeps" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="Test runner." \
      org.opencontainers.image.licenses="MIT"
WORKDIR /work
USER 65534:65534

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# The harness's CI steps (spec side). tools/record.py runs them as the
# C-HARNESS-* checks, and skips them where harness/ isn't on disk.
#
#   harness/ci.sh tag                print the local image tag
#   harness/ci.sh image              build the runtime image (and print the
#                                    fwtest binary's SHA-256)
#   harness/ci.sh test               build the test stage: cargo test
#   harness/ci.sh suite OUT MOUNT    run tests/harness.suite in a fresh
#                                    container, harness/tests mounted
#                                    read-only at MOUNT; outputs in OUT
#   harness/ci.sh scope              the harness never uses the vendored
#                                    crates' stock-boot path or other boards
#                                    (packages only through their reader)
#   harness/ci.sh context            write the build context (a tar) to stdout
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PLATFORM=linux/amd64

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$@"
    else shasum -a 256 "$@"; fi
}

# The image tag: a hash of everything that goes into the build context.
tag() {
    h=$(cd "$ROOT" && context_files | LC_ALL=C sort | while read -r f; do sha256 "$f"; done | sha256 | cut -c1-16)
    echo "small-beeps-fwtest:$h"
}

# (The spec-side experiments are not part of fwtest: harness/spec-experiments/
# runs them against it.)
context_files() {
    git -C "$ROOT" ls-files vendor/emulator harness LICENSE NOTICE | grep -v '^harness/spec-experiments/'
}

# A tar of exactly the tracked context files (its owners and times don't
# matter: the build's outputs don't depend on them).
context() {
    cd "$ROOT"
    context_files | LC_ALL=C sort > "$tmp/files"
    tar --format=ustar -c -f - -T "$tmp/files" 2>/dev/null \
        || tar -c -f - $(cat "$tmp/files")
}

build() {
    target=$1 t=$2
    context | docker build --platform "$PLATFORM" --target "$target" -t "$t" -f harness/Dockerfile -
}

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

case "${1:-}" in
    tag) tag ;;
    context) context ;;
    image)
        t=$(tag)
        build runtime "$t"
        docker image inspect --format 'image {{.Id}}' "$t"
        docker run --rm --platform "$PLATFORM" --network none --entrypoint sha256sum "$t" /usr/local/bin/fwtest
        docker run --rm --platform "$PLATFORM" --network none "$t" version ;;
    test)
        build test "$(tag)-test" ;;
    suite)
        out=$2 mount=$3
        t=$(tag)
        docker image inspect "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1 || build runtime "$t"
        rm -rf "$out"
        mkdir -p "$out"
        out=$(cd "$out" && pwd)
        docker run --rm --platform "$PLATFORM" --network none --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
            -v "$ROOT/harness/tests:$mount:ro" -v "$out:/out" "$t" \
            suite "$mount/harness.suite" --out /out/suite ;;
    scope)
        # file names and counts only: CI logs must not quote harness or emulator source
        # since A1 a package goes through the reader (fwsc::unpack) and the boot
        # block (write_boot_info) only, never the stock path's extras
        if grep -c -E 'stock_from_package|stock_boot|usr_fill_defaults|usr_load_syx|usr_offset|smk|Smk37|flaky' "$ROOT"/harness/src/*.rs | grep -v ':0$'; then
            echo "scope: FAIL, the harness names the stock-boot or other-board paths" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        if grep -o -h -E 'fwsc::[a-z_]+' "$ROOT"/harness/src/*.rs | sort -u | grep -v -x -E 'fwsc::unpack'; then
            echo "scope: FAIL, the harness uses more of the package module than its reader" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        echo "scope: PASS (harness/src uses none of them)" ;;
    *) sed -n '5,18p' "$0" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

### SR-7: fwtest doesn't run a two-register load the compiler emits (a harness gap)
- Asked: 2026-10-23, session M5 (firmware side)
- Question: fwtest ends a run as a fault ("an instruction the emulator
  does not implement") at the two-register load that moves its address
  down first, which the toolchain's disassembler prints as
  `{r3, r0} = [-r4]` (bytes `44 eb 09 00`). Please make fwtest run it,
  and its kin if the encoding has them (other register pairs, the store
  `[-rN] = {rA, rB}`, a post-incrementing form), as the chip does, and
  say in HARNESS.md or HARDWARE-SPEC.md which forms fwtest runs. This is
  about fwtest only, not the hardware: the compiler emits the form on its
  own, with or without `-mcpu=r3 -mfprev1`.
- Where it came from: M5's FM engine. clang (the pinned toolchain,
  P-1), `-target pi32v2 -mcpu=r3 -mfprev1 -std=c11 -ffreestanding -Os`
  (tools/build.sh), made one of it in `voice_start()` in
  `firmware/src/fm_play.c`, from seven consecutive word copies of one
  struct's array fields into another's (`o->step[0..3] =
  p->op[i].step[0..3]; o->target[0..2] = ...`). The same file built with
  the toolchain's default CPU and no float flag gives the same
  instruction. The engine's first fwtest run faulted there on core 0.
- Minimal reproduction (our own code; assembled with the pinned clang,
  `-target pi32v2 -mcpu=r3`, linked at `0x02000000`, raw image from
  `.text`, run with `tools/fwtest run IMAGE --ms 1 --ram
  0x01c00020:12@end`):

  ```
  _start:
  	r4 = 0x01C00010
  	r1 = 0x29F3A1C5
  	[r4+-8] = r1
  	r1 = 0x7E41D60B
  	[r4+-4] = r1
  	{r3, r0} = [-r4]
  	r5 = 0x01C00020
  	[r5+0] = r0
  	[r5+4] = r3
  	[r5+8] = r4
  	cli
  1:	goto 1b
  ```

  fwtest: exit 3, `fault`, "core 0 at pc 0x02000016: an instruction the
  emulator does not implement", nothing stored. The control image, the
  same with `r4 += -8; r0 = [r4+0]; r3 = [r4+4]` in place of the one
  instruction: exit 4, `halt` as meant, and the stores show r0
  `0x29F3A1C5`, r3 `0x7E41D60B`, r4 `0x01C00008`, which is what we expect
  the one instruction to leave (which register gets which word is part of
  the question).
- Workaround until then: `voice_start()` copies those fields a word at a
  time through a volatile pointer (`copy_words`, fm_play.c), and
  tools/build.sh fails an image whose disassembly holds the form, so
  none reaches fwtest unnoticed (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M5). Both go once
  fwtest runs it.
- Status: answered (HARDWARE-SPEC.md, "15. Block moves with a register
  base (SR-7)", HW-66; docs/HARNESS.md, "Instructions"): the encoding has
  eight modes, loads and stores, up or below the base, with or without
  moving it, for any base and any list of r0 to r15; fwtest 0.3.0 runs all
  eight. The lowest register takes the lowest address, so your r0 and r3
  are right, but the form without `--` leaves the base as it was: r4 stays
  `0x01C00010`, not `0x01C00008` (the compiler's own code relies on this).
  The compiler emits the forms without `++` / `--`; the others, and a base
  that is also in a write-back form's list, are open for the chip (Q-19).
  A corpus check of what the compiler emits for the firmware's flags,
  across registers and immediates, found two more forms fwtest doesn't
  run: a rotate by a register, which the compiler emits, and a 4-byte push
  or pop of a list not starting at r0, which it was not seen to emit
  (HARNESS.md, "Instructions", "Known gaps"). Since fwtest 0.4.0
  (2026-10-24, session emulator-parity) both run (HARNESS.md,
  "Instructions").
  fwtest 0.3.0 reaches `tools/fwtest` when the pull request after this
  one pins its image; then `copy_words` and build.sh's check can go.
- Answered: 2026-10-24, session SR-7 (spec side)

- Fact: The F-Emulator app loads a package through the emulator crates'
  package reader, their conversion to the flash image and their stock
  boot, all unchanged from upstream `43ed558`, so a package boots in it as
  in the upstream web build (HW-93's checks and boot). Around them, the
  app adds checks of its own:
  1. Before the reader, it refuses, with a message, a file over 16 MiB, a
     package under 960 bytes or over 8 MiB, a catalog download whose
     SHA-256 differs from the catalog's, and an M-VAVE version newer than
     015 (by the package's own name).
  2. A package that crashes the reader is refused as malformed.
  3. It loads no patch bank of its own into the user-patch area (`USR`,
     HW-80); the defaults are filled as upstream does.
  4. After boot, the firmware's own saved flash sectors are written over
     the image, after checks: whole 4 KiB sectors, in range, none
     repeated.
  It then runs the interpreted CPU, with idle skipping, each firmware at
  its own measured clock. This settles HW-93's "for the owner to confirm".
- Sources: the app session's own description of its path, behaviour only,
  relayed by the owner on 2026-10-27 (recorded by session spec-1027; this
  side doesn't open the app's branch); EMULATOR-PARITY.md, "Packages".

Each has a budget per milestone in `config/budgets.json` (R-PERF-1). Steady-state instructions per period may also not rise by more than 3% against the latest record of a main commit made under the same steady-state budget, whose own image is re-measured with the same fwtest, runs and options; against a record made under another budget (or none) the change is reported and not gated. Since M3 a record made under the current steady-state budget is a baseline only if its firmware image (SHA-256) differs from that of the last record before the budget was raised: records that still hold the pre-raise image (the raise's own merge, or any merge after it that changed no firmware) are skipped and named in the baseline note, so the order records are written in doesn't matter. (Briefly in M3, before this rule: the first record made under a budget was not compared.) A fall of more than 3% is reported in the record and the pull request's checks. Startup has no 3% gate. No noise allowance: the count is deterministic. Until audio (M4) the period is the heartbeat (one beat per millisecond); from M4 it is the audio block (64 stereo frames, 1.451 ms), counted by fwtest as the rows of `ipb.csv`, and an image with no audio output (one from before M4) has no period, so a baseline made of one is reported, not compared. Until M2 the measure was one one-second run's instructions over its beats, startup included. Since M4b (the owner's request) a **loaded** measure as well: the same two runs with a fixed input script (`tests/fw/scripts/perfload.txt`, its SHA-256 in the record) that drives the firmware to its heaviest steady load, every voice sounding and every control moving, with a pattern that repeats a whole number of times between the runs' ends; its steady state per period is worked out the same way. NAME (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) is the case's output folder under DIR.
EXPECT is the outcome expected: `completed`, `halt`, `fault`, `hang` or
`power-cut`. A
case passes when its outcome is EXPECT and every golden file matches. DIR
also gets `result.json` (every case's result) and `junit.xml` (one test case
per suite case). The exit code is 0 when every case passes, 1 otherwise, 2
on a usage error.

## Determinism

The same image, script, options and fwtest build give byte-identical outputs
on every run and every machine: no host time, no randomness that isn't
seeded the same way every run, nothing from the environment, no host paths
in the results. CI runs the harness's own suite twice in fresh containers
and compares every output byte (C-HARNESS-DET). If two runs of yours ever
differ, that is a bug in fwtest: report it.

## Versions

`fwtest version` prints fwtest's version and the emulator build it carries;
`result.json` has both. The image is identified by its digest. When the
harness changes, a pull request moves `config/fwtest-image` to the new
digest, so a firmware test always names the exact runner it used.

- 0.8.0: update packages: `--package` boots a `.fwsc` through the
  emulator's package path, with fwtest's own checks ("Packages").
  Its pin is the clean side's pull request too, opened once the image is
  published (the owner's answer, recorded by session spec-answers-a1).
- 0.7.0: the USB core's register access port answers at once (bit 15
  set), a read giving the byte last written to its index and the
  interrupt flags 0 ("USB").

git checkout -q -b spec/1027-image-repro && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='harness/ci.sh'; s=open(p).read()
def rep(o,n):
    global s; assert s.count(o)==1,o; s=s.replace(o,n)
rep("""#   harness/ci.sh test               build the test stage: cargo test
""","""#   harness/ci.sh test               build the test stage: cargo test
#   harness/ci.sh repro              build the runtime image twice from
#                                    scratch, the second time at another
#                                    time and from a context whose file
#                                    times and owners differ: the same
#                                    image ID, or a failure
""")
rep("""# A tar of exactly the tracked context files (its owners and times don't
# matter: the build's outputs don't depend on them).
context() {
    cd "$ROOT"
    context_files | LC_ALL=C sort > "$tmp/files"
    tar --format=ustar -c -f - -T "$tmp/files" 2>/dev/null \\
        || tar -c -f - $(cat "$tmp/files")
}

build() {
    target=$1 t=$2
    context | docker build --platform "$PLATFORM" --target "$target" -t "$t" -f harness/Dockerfile -
}
""","""# A tar of exactly the tracked context files (its owners and times don't
# matter: the build's outputs don't depend on them, and the image's file
# times are rewritten, below).
context() {
    cd "$ROOT"
    context_files | LC_ALL=C sort > "$tmp/files"
    tar --format=ustar -c -f - -T "$tmp/files" 2>/dev/null \\
        || tar -c -f - $(cat "$tmp/files")
}

# The image's one time, the Dockerfile's SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. Passed as a build
# argument, BuildKit gives it to the image's config and history, and
# rewrite-timestamp clamps every file time in the new layers to it, so the
# build's time and the checkout's file times never reach the image. No
# provenance attestation: it records the build's own times. (Before this, two
# builds of the same source gave the same files under other times, so another
# digest: session spec-1027.)
epoch() {
    sed -n 's/^.*SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=\\([0-9][0-9]*\\).*$/\\1/p' "$ROOT/harness/Dockerfile" | head -n 1
}

build() {
    target=$1 t=$2
    shift 2
    e=$(epoch)
    [ -n "$e" ] || { echo "no SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH in harness/Dockerfile" >&2; exit 1; }
    context | docker build --platform "$PLATFORM" --target "$target" --provenance=false \\
        --build-arg SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH="$e" --output "type=docker,name=$t,rewrite-timestamp=true" \\
        "$@" -f harness/Dockerfile -

# source gives the same image, whenever and wherever it is built (harness/ci.sh
# repro; session spec-1027 found two 0.7.0 images that differed in times only).""")
rep("""#   test     runs the harness's own tests (cargo test)
#   runtime  the published image: Debian slim, the binary, the licences""","""#   test     runs the harness's own tests (cargo test)
#   files    the runtime image's own files, their owners, modes and times set
#   runtime  the published image: Debian slim, the binary, the licences""")
rep("""FROM --platform=linux/amd64 ${BASE} AS runtime

COPY --chown=0:0 LICENSE /usr/share/doc/fwtest/LICENSE
COPY --chown=0:0 NOTICE /usr/share/doc/fwtest/NOTICE
COPY --chown=0:0 vendor/emulator/LICENSE /usr/share/doc/fwtest/LICENSE.emulator
""","""FROM --platform=linux/amd64 ${BASE} AS files
ARG SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
COPY --from=build /src/harness/target/release/fwtest /out/usr/local/bin/fwtest
COPY LICENSE NOTICE /out/usr/share/doc/fwtest/
COPY vendor/emulator/LICENSE /out/usr/share/doc/fwtest/LICENSE.emulator

 && mkdir -p /out/work \\
 && chown -R 0:0 /out \\

 && find /out -type f -exec chmod 0644 {} + \\
 && chmod 0755 /out/usr/local/bin/fwtest \\
 && find /out -exec touch -h -d "@$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH" {} +

FROM --platform=linux/amd64 ${BASE} AS runtime
COPY --from=files /out/ /
""")

p='harness/ci.sh'; s=open(p).read()

# attestation: it records the build's own times. (Before this, two builds of

p='harness/ci.sh'; s=open(p).read()
o="""# The context again, every file an hour newer and owned by another user.
shifted_context() {
    tracked_context | python3 -I -c '
import sys, tarfile
src = tarfile.open(fileobj=sys.stdin.buffer, mode="r|")
dst = tarfile.open(fileobj=sys.stdout.buffer, mode="w|", format=tarfile.USTAR_FORMAT)
for m in src:
    data = src.extractfile(m) if m.isfile() else None
    m.mtime += 3600
    m.uid, m.gid, m.uname, m.gname = 4321, 4321, "", ""
    dst.addfile(m, data)
dst.close()'
}"""
n="""# The context again, as the file $tmp/shifted.tar: every file an hour newer
# and owned by another user.
shifted_context() {
    tracked_context > "$tmp/context.tar"
    python3 -I -c '
import sys, tarfile
src = tarfile.open(sys.argv[1], mode="r:")
dst = tarfile.open(sys.argv[2], mode="w", format=tarfile.USTAR_FORMAT)
for m in src:
    data = src.extractfile(m) if m.isfile() else None
    m.mtime += 3600
    m.uid, m.gid, m.uname, m.gname = 4321, 4321, "", ""
    dst.addfile(m, data)
dst.close()' "$tmp/context.tar" "$tmp/shifted.tar"
}"""
assert s.count(o)==1; s=s.replace(o,n)
o="""        sleep 2
        context() { shifted_context; }"""
n="""        sleep 2
        shifted_context
        context() { cat "$tmp/shifted.tar"; }"""
assert s.count(o)==1; s=s.replace(o,n)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Builds everything inside the pinned build container (tools/Dockerfile).
#
#   tools/build.sh image                      build the container image
#   tools/build.sh image-tag                  print its tag
#   tools/build.sh build --out DIR [--src-mount PATH] [--define NAME]...
#                        [--demo plaits]
#                                             build in a fresh container,
#                                             outputs and SHA256SUMS in DIR;
#                                             --define adds -DNAME (test
#                                             builds only, tools/perf.py);
#                                             --demo builds a demo's own
#                                             image instead (M4b: the
#                                             Plaits load test), never the
#                                             firmware's
#   tools/build.sh inside SRC OUT             (runs inside the container)
#
# The outputs: app.elf and app.bin (the raw image, linked at 0x02000000),
# app.size, and since A1 (not for --demo) app-pkg.elf and app-pkg.bin, the
# same objects linked at 0x02000120 for a .fwsc (tools/fwsc.py; HW-91).
#
# Builds are deterministic (R-REPRO-3): fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (set in the
# image), no network, relative source paths with -fdebug-prefix-map, sorted
# output lists, and a check that no output contains the source mount path.
homebrew
#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Builds the harness's own test images with the pinned toolchain container
# (tools/build.sh image) and writes SHA256SUMS.
#
#   harness/tests/images/build.sh            build into this folder
#   harness/tests/images/build.sh --check    build into a temporary folder
#                                            and compare with the committed
#                                            images (C-HARNESS-IMAGES)
#   harness/tests/images/build.sh inside OUT (runs inside the container)
# C with code in RAM (image-ram.ld, flash.h)
# built with the firmware's CPU flags (tools/build.sh, CPU), as the firmware is
# C linked where a package's app runs (image-pkg.ld), for tests/package.rs
# assembly, linked after start.S like the C images
# assembly with its own _start, linked alone
    clang -target pi32v2 -c start.S -o "$out/start.o"
        clang $flags -c "$n.c" -o "$out/$n.o"

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Vendors three crates of the public emulator upstream, at a pinned commit,
# into vendor/emulator/, applies the patches in vendor/emulator/patches/, and
# checks every file against vendor/emulator/SHA256SUMS, whose own SHA-256 is
# the tree hash below (PROVENANCE P-7). Spec side only: vendor/emulator/ is
# left out of clean folders, and --fetch refuses to run in one.
#
#   tools/fetch-emulator.sh --verify   check the committed files (default,
#                                      offline; SKIP when vendor/emulator/
#                                      isn't on disk, as in a clean folder)
#   tools/fetch-emulator.sh --fetch    re-download them from the pinned commit,
#                                      apply the patches, then verify
#
# The fetch is a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout of exactly the paths
# in UPSTREAM_PATHS, so nothing else in that repository reaches the disk.
# To move to another commit: change UPSTREAM_COMMIT, run --fetch in a spec
# folder, rewrite SHA256SUMS (--sums), update TREE_SHA256 and UPSTREAM.md,
# and log it in PROVENANCE.md, all in one pull request.
# SHA-256 of vendor/emulator/SHA256SUMS: one hash for the whole tree.
# Ours, not upstream's: not listed in SHA256SUMS.
When both halves of a dual-issue pair write the same register, the head's
result is the one there after the pair. Upstream kept the second half's.
The vendor compiler relies on the head's: it pairs a head computing a
value with a word load into the same register whose result it doesn't
use (an unused read of SPI0's BUF), then uses the register as the head's
value, as in

    r7 = r6 + 0x80000  #
    r7 = [r1+8]
    r5 = r7 >> 16

(flash routines at -Os) and `r0 = r1.b0 (u) #` or `r0 = uextra(...) #`
with `r0 = [r3+8]`, then `[r3+8] = r0` (at -O2). Of every pair in the
firmware at main's 6ba587e, the harness's test images and the spec
experiments (at -Os and -O2), these are the only ones whose halves write
one register, and each uses the head's value next; none uses the second
half's. Limit: a head that leaves a register's value as it was can't be
told from one that didn't write it, so the second half's value stays
there.

Our own change (session day-1024, 2026-10-24), from the vendor
toolchain's code (PROVENANCE P-1). The crate test
pair_head_wins_over_its_second_half and the harness test of the same
name (image tests/images/pairwaw.S) fail without it; the firmware's
suite at 6ba587e gives the same outputs with and without it.

}

listed_files() {
    (cd "$DEST" && find . -type f | sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort) | while read -r f; do
        case " $OURS " in *" $f "*) continue ;; esac
        printf '%s\n' "$f"
    done
}

verify() {
    if [ ! -d "$DEST" ]; then
        echo "SKIP: vendor/emulator/ is not on disk (a clean folder leaves it out)"
        return 0
    fi
    status=0
    got=$(sha256 "$SUMS")
    if [ "$got" = "$TREE_SHA256" ]; then echo "OK      SHA256SUMS (tree hash $TREE_SHA256)"
    else echo "CHANGED SHA256SUMS ($got, want $TREE_SHA256)"; status=1; fi
    while read -r want path; do
        [ -n "$want" ] || continue
        if [ ! -f "$DEST/$path" ]; then
            echo "MISSING $path"; status=1; continue
        fi
        [ "$(sha256 "$DEST/$path")" = "$want" ] || { echo "CHANGED $path"; status=1; }
    done < "$SUMS"
    for f in $(listed_files); do
        if ! awk -v p="$f" '$2 == p { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' "$SUMS"; then
            echo "UNLISTED $f"; status=1
        fi
    done
    n=$(grep -c . "$SUMS")
    if [ $status -eq 0 ]; then echo "$n emulator files match commit $UPSTREAM_COMMIT plus patches"; fi
    return $status
}

sums() {
    (cd "$DEST" && for f in $(listed_files); do printf '%s  %s\n' "$(sha256 "$f")" "$f"; done) > "$SUMS"
    echo "wrote SHA256SUMS: tree hash $(sha256 "$SUMS")"
}

refuse_in_clean_folder() {
    role=$(cat "$ROOT/.claude/small-beeps-role" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ "$role" = clean ] || git -C "$ROOT" sparse-checkout list 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^!/vendor/emulator/'; then
        echo "REFUSED: this is a clean folder; emulator source must never reach it." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
}

fetch() {
    refuse_in_clean_folder
    work=$(mktemp -d)
    trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
    git -C "$work" init -q
    git -C "$work" remote add origin "$UPSTREAM_URL"
    git -C "$work" fetch -q --depth 1 --filter=blob:none origin "$UPSTREAM_COMMIT"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    git -C "$work" sparse-checkout set --no-cone $UPSTREAM_PATHS
    git -C "$work" -c advice.detachedHead=false checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
    got=$(git -C "$work" rev-parse HEAD)
    [ "$got" = "$UPSTREAM_COMMIT" ] || { echo "fetched $got, want $UPSTREAM_COMMIT"; exit 1; }
    for p in $(ls "$DEST/patches"/*.patch 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        git -C "$work" apply --whitespace=nowarn "$p"
        echo "applied $(basename "$p")"
    done
    keep=$(mktemp -d)
    for f in $OURS patches; do [ -e "$DEST/$f" ] && cp -R "$DEST/$f" "$keep/"; done
    rm -rf "$DEST"
    mkdir -p "$DEST/crates"
    cp "$work/LICENSE" "$work/Cargo.toml" "$DEST/"
    for c in fm1-isa fm1-core fm1-soc; do cp -R "$work/crates/$c" "$DEST/crates/"; done
    for f in $OURS patches; do [ -e "$keep/$f" ] && cp -R "$keep/$f" "$DEST/"; done
    rm -rf "$keep"
    verify
}

case "${1:---verify}" in
    --verify) verify ;;
    --fetch) fetch ;;
    --sums) sums ;;
    *) echo "usage: $0 [--verify|--fetch|--sums]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

   word, halfword and byte, an immediate or a register step, the 2-byte
   short forms). The vendor compiler emits them for C that stores the base
   as it was (`q = p + 187; *q = p;` gives `[++r0=748] = r0`, and never for

HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)
IMAGES="heartbeat halt wild hang console lcd leds keys pot midi midiout audio spi1irq usbport"
# C with code in RAM (image-ram.ld, flash.h)
RAM_IMAGES="flashrw flashcall flashload flashirq flashkeep flashhelper"
# built with the firmware's CPU flags (tools/build.sh, CPU), as the firmware is
FW_IMAGES="blockc rotc"
# C linked where a package's app runs (image-pkg.ld), for tests/package.rs
PKG_IMAGES="pkgapp"
# assembly, linked after start.S like the C images
ASM_IMAGES="blockmv pairhead rotr pushpop ramcode pairwaw"
# assembly with its own _start, linked alone
RAW_IMAGES="sr7"
ALL="$IMAGES $RAM_IMAGES $FW_IMAGES $PKG_IMAGES $ASM_IMAGES $RAW_IMAGES"

inside() {
    out=$1
    cd "$HERE"
    flags="-target pi32v2 -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -Os -Wall -Wextra -Werror"
    clang -target pi32v2 -c start.S -o "$out/start.o"
    for n in $IMAGES; do
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        clang $flags -c "$n.c" -o "$out/$n.o"
        ld -nostdlib -T image.ld -o "$out/$n.elf" "$out/start.o" "$out/$n.o"
        objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/$n.elf" "$out/$n.bin"
        rm "$out/$n.o" "$out/$n.elf"
    # blockc exists for the two forms below a base the compiler emits (SR-7)
    if ! grep -q '} = \[-r[0-9]*\]' "$out/blockc.dis" || ! grep -q '\[-r[0-9]*\] = {' "$out/blockc.dis"; then
        echo "blockc: the compiler no longer emits {..} = [-rN] and [-rN] = {..}" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    # rotc exists for the rotate by a register the compiler emits
    if ! grep -q 'r[0-9]* = r[0-9]* <> r[0-9]*$' "$out/rotc.dis"; then
        echo "rotc: the compiler no longer emits rD = rS <> rT" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    # pairwaw.S stands for a pair whose halves write one register, which the
    # compiler emits in flashkeep.c (a head, then a load into the same register)
    if ! awk -F '\t' '$NF ~ /^r[0-9]+ = .*# *$/ { h = $NF; sub(/ .*/, "", h); next }
              h != "" { t = $NF; sub(/^ */, "", t); if (index(t, h " = [") == 1) found = 1; h = "" }
              END { exit !found }' "$out/flashkeep.dis"; then
        echo "flashkeep: the compiler no longer pairs a head and a load into one register" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    for n in $FW_IMAGES $RAM_IMAGES; do rm "$out/$n.dis"; done
    for n in $ASM_IMAGES; do
        clang -target pi32v2 -mcpu=r3 -c "$n.S" -o "$out/$n.o"
        ld -nostdlib -T image.ld -o "$out/$n.elf" "$out/start.o" "$out/$n.o"
        objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/$n.elf" "$out/$n.bin"
        rm "$out/$n.o" "$out/$n.elf"
    done
    for n in $RAW_IMAGES; do
        clang -target pi32v2 -mcpu=r3 -c "$n.S" -o "$out/$n.o"
        ld -nostdlib -T image.ld -o "$out/$n.elf" "$out/$n.o"
        objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/$n.elf" "$out/$n.bin"
        rm "$out/$n.o" "$out/$n.elf"
    done

typedef unsigned int u32;

#define REG(a) (*(volatile u32 *)(a))

#define OUTBUF ((volatile unsigned char *)0x01c00200u)

#define VECTOR(n) REG(0x01c7fe00u + 4u * (n))

#define ICFG(n) REG(0x1eef100u + 4u * ((n) >> 3))
#define ICFG_ON(n, prio) (((1u | ((prio) << 1)) & 0xfu) << (((n) & 7u) * 4u))

input.command:
{ cat <<'EOF'
A store with a base update whose stored register is the base itself
stores the base as it was before the instruction, as a post-increment
already did. Upstream moved a pre-increment's base first and then read
the source, so `[++r4=748] = r4` stored the moved base (the word,
halfword and byte forms with an immediate step; a register step already
read the source first). The vendor compiler relies on the old value: for

    int *f(int *p) { int *q = p + 187; *q = (int)p; return q; }

it emits the one instruction `[++r0=748] = r0`, and for the same with
`*q = (int)q` (the moved base) it never uses the form, computing the new
base in another register. Its assembler takes every such form without a
word. Found by a firmware built on small-beeps, which faulted in fwtest
on `[++r4=748] = r4` (bytes d2 ec 4f 4e) depending only on register
allocation (SR-10).

Our own change (session spec-1027, 2026-10-27), from the vendor
toolchain's code (PROVENANCE P-1). What the chip stores is not
established without a unit (HARDWARE-SPEC Q-27). Loads into the base
register and register pairs that hold their base (Q-19) are unchanged.
The crate test stores_of_the_base_keep_its_old_value and the harness
test of the same name (images tests/images/selfstore.S and selfc.c) fail
without it.

EOF
git diff --relative=vendor/emulator -- vendor/emulator/crates/fm1-core/src/lib.rs; } > vendor/emulator/patches/0013-store-of-the-base-keeps-its-old-value.patch; head -c 0 /dev/null; grep -c "^@@" vendor/emulator/patches/0013-store-of-the-base-keeps-its-old-value.patch; grep -n "TREE_SHA256=" tools/fetch-emulator.sh; sed -n 1,80p vendor/emulator/UPSTREAM.md | grep -n "0012\|0011\|^#" | head

"Merge pull request #39 from joakimeriksson/windows-jit", committed
  2026-10-21T22:07:20+02:00)
- Licence: MIT, copyright 2026 Joakim Eriksson (`LICENSE` here, copied
  unmodified).
- What: `crates/fm1-isa`, `crates/fm1-core` and `crates/fm1-soc`, at the
  same paths, unmodified but for the patches below (0002 to 0012: bug
  fixes, two speed-only changes and MIDI out) and the workspace manifest
  `Cargo.toml` (patched, 0001). docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md compares them with
  the F-Emulator app's.
  Nothing else from that repository: no other crates, no `fm1-sid/`, no
  probes, no firmware files.
  `harness/upstream/fm1-emu-pair-same-register.md` describe them (fwtest
  0.6.0). (Listed here by session spec-overnight-1025.)
- `patches/0012-usb-port-answers.patch` (session spec-overnight-1025,
  2026-10-26; the F-Emulator app's change, from its behaviour-only note,
  PROVENANCE P-59): `crates/fm1-soc/src/lib.rs`, the USB core's access
  port at 0x11804 (`JL_USB->CON1`): reading it gives the last value
  written with bit 15 (`MACK`, done) set; for a read (bit 14 set)
  bits 0-7 hold the byte last written to that index, the interrupt flags
  (indexes 2-6) 0. Upstream kept the word as plain storage, so a firmware
  waited out its own timeout on every access. The crate test and the
  harness test `usb_port_answers` (image `tests/images/usbport.c`, suite
  case `usbport`) fail without it (`harness/upstream/fm1-emu-usb-port.md`;
  fwtest 0.7.0). Licence: the owner confirmed the note is covered by MIT
  on the same terms as P-47 (recorded by session spec-a1-fwsc).

0007 and 0008 change no output: the firmware suite, the spec experiments
and the harness suite gave byte-identical outputs (284 files) from fwtest
built with and without them (docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md).

## Not used

The harness never calls the crates' update-package and stock-boot paths
(`fwsc`, `stock_from_package`, `stock_boot`, `write_boot_info`); they are
vendored only because the crate is kept whole. C-HARNESS-SCOPE checks
that `harness/src` names none of them.

### HW-66: The block moves with a register base, and fwtest
- Fact: a 4-byte instruction moves the registers in a list to or from
  consecutive words at a base register: bytes `xm eb` then a 16-bit
  register mask, low byte first (bit k: register rk, r0 to r15). In the
  first byte, bits 0 to 3 are the base register and bits 4 to 6 the mode;
  bit 7 must be 0 (with it set the bytes are a different instruction).
  The toolchain writes the eight modes as:
  - `0x0`: `{list} = [rN+]`, `0x1`: `{list} = [rN++]`,
    `0x2`: `[rN+] = {list}`, `0x3`: `[rN++] = {list}`;
  - `0x4`: `{list} = [-rN]`, `0x5`: `{list} = [--rN]`,
    `0x6`: `[-rN] = {list}`, `0x7`: `[--rN] = {list}`.

  Mode bit 4 is the `++` / `--` form, bit 5 a store, bit 6 a block below
  the base. With n registers in the list: the lowest-numbered register
  takes the lowest address; `[rN+]` and `[rN++]` cover the n words from
  rN up, `[-rN]` and `[--rN]` the n words just below rN (rN - 4n to
  rN - 4). Without `++` / `--` the base keeps its value, and every address
  comes from the base as it was, so a base that is also in a loaded list
  ends with its loaded word. The toolchain's compiler emits `[rN+]` and
  `[-rN]`, loads and stores, on its own (SR-7's `{r3, r0} = [-r4]` is mode
  `0x4`, mask `0x0009`): SR-7's reproduction leaves r0 `0x29F3A1C5`, r3
  `0x7E41D60B` and r4 `0x01C00010`, unchanged. `[rN++]` and `[--rN]` are
  assembler forms the compiler was not seen to emit; fwtest runs them with
  the base moved past the block (rN + 4n, rN - 4n). fwtest runs all eight
  modes this way since 0.3.0 (HARNESS, "Instructions"); before, `[-rN]` and
  `[--rN]` ended the run as a fault. On the chip, what `[rN++]` and
  `[--rN]` leave in the base, a write-back form whose base is also in its
  list, and an empty list, are open (Q-19).

  mask tried (the encoding); the compiler's code for C with known results,

## Instructions

fwtest runs the code the pinned toolchain's compiler emits for the
firmware's flags (`-target pi32v2 -mcpu=r3 -mfprev1`, tools/build.sh);
the two gaps the checks below found run since 0.4.0. That was checked on a corpus, not proven for
every instruction (SR-7). The corpus: the firmware at `18d9459`, the
vendored Plaits and the demo's C++ built with the firmware's CPU flags,
and several hundred small C functions written to vary types, operations
and pointer patterns, each at `-Os` and `-O2`. Two checks ran in fwtest
0.3.0, each unit on its own:

- every distinct disassembled unit of the corpus's objects (13 981; a
  dual-issue pair is one unit; some are constants in the code, decoded
  as if they were instructions);
- every form in the compiler's assembly output (660, registers and numbers
  abstracted), with each register slot set in turn to r0 to r15 (register
  pairs to each even-odd pair) and each number to values from 0 and ±1 up
  to the 32-bit limits, as far as the assembler accepts them: 34 437
  distinct encodings.

They show only that fwtest decodes and runs each one, not that it
computes what the chip does. An instruction neither check held can still
end a run as a fault ("Outcomes and exit codes"): report it as SR-7 was,
with its bytes and the smallest image that shows it.

No known gaps since fwtest 0.6.0 (0.5.0 and earlier: the pairs below,
"Both halves writing one register"). In 0.3.0 and earlier two forms ended the run as
a fault, "an instruction the emulated CPU cannot decode"; 0.4.0 runs them,
and one more change makes dual-issue pairs behave as the compiler expects:

- **Rotate by a register.** `rD = rS <> rT` (bytes `cc e1`, then two
  bytes naming the registers; `cc f1` as a pair's head), for every
  register. It rotates right by rT: the compiler emits
  `(x << s) | (x >> (32 - s))` as `rT = 32 - rT` then this, and
  `(x >> 7) | (x << 25)` as the rotate by a constant `rD = rS <> 7`. By
  0 it leaves the value (the compiler's masked rotate relies on that). An
  amount of 32 or more is taken mod 32, which the compiler's code doesn't
  show (it masks such amounts itself): don't rely on it.
- **A 4-byte push or pop of any register list.** `[--sp] = {list}` (bytes
  `d8 e8`, then the 16-bit mask, bit k for rk) and `{list} = [sp++]`
  (`d4 e8`, then the mask), without `rets` or `pc`: every list, for
  example `[--sp] = {r5-r1}`, `{r11-r6} = [sp++]` or `{r15} = [sp++]`, as
  the lists from r0 already ran. A push moves sp down by 4 a register and
  the lowest register takes the lowest address; a pop reads them back the
  same way. The compiler emits only lists from r0 (in interrupt
  handlers); lists above r0 behave the same by analogy, not checked
  against the chip.
- **Dual-issue pairs** (`A #` then `B`, as the toolchain's disassembler
  prints them): the pair's second half sees the registers as they were
  before the head, and the head's result is there after the pair. The
  compiler relies on this (in our firmware, a pair whose second half
  stores a byte back through the base register the head changes). In
  0.3.0 and earlier some 4-byte ALU forms as a pair's head wrote their result at
  once, so the second half saw the new value: which ones depended on the
  operation and the registers (of one of each family with the same
  registers, two: `r6 = r5 ^ (1 << r3) #` and `r6 = r5 >>> r3 #`).

None of the three changed any output of the firmware's suite at `cdfd067`.

**Both halves writing one register (0.6.0).** When both halves of a
dual-issue pair write the same register, the head's result is the one
there after the pair, as the compiler's code expects: it pairs a head
computing a value with a load into the same register whose result it
doesn't use, then uses the head's value (seen in flash routines:
`rA = rB + 0x80000 #` then `rA = [rC+8]`, an unused read of SPI0's
`BUF`, then `rA` as the address). fwtest 0.5.0 kept the second half's
value, so such code computed the wrong address or value there. A head
whose result equals the register's old value can't be told from one that
didn't write it; then the second half's value stays. The firmware's suite
at `6ba587e` gives the same outputs with and without the change.

### Block moves with a register base

# Upstream note: a dual-issue pair whose halves write one register

For the owner to apply in the F-Emulator app, and to offer to
`joakimeriksson/fm1-emu` if wanted. Spec side only; not filed by a
session. Written in session day-1024 (2026-10-24) against commit
`43ed5580064885e93bc8d20be931ae950d10cd4f`; our copy carries the change as
`vendor/emulator/patches/0011-pair-head-wins-over-its-second-half.patch`
(fwtest 0.6.0). docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md lists it.

## What upstream does

`fm1-core` holds a pair head's register results until the second half has
run, then commits those the second half didn't change. When both halves
write the same register, the second half's value stays.

## What the vendor compiler expects

The head's. It pairs a head computing a value with a word load into the
same register whose result it doesn't use, then uses the register as the
head's value:

```
r7 = r6 + 0x80000  #
r7 = [r1+8]
r5 = r7 >> 16
```

(an unused read of SPI0's `BUF` in a flash routine at `-Os`; at `-O2` also
`r0 = r1.b0 (u) #` and `r0 = uextra(r1, p:8, l:8) #` with `r0 = [r3+8]`,
then `[r3+8] = r0`). In everything we compiled, these are the only pairs
whose halves write one register, and each uses the head's value next.

## What the patch does

Both commit loops (`step` and `exec_fast_paired`) commit every register
the head changed, over the second half's write. The JIT needs nothing: the
block builder glues a pair into compiled code only when the head's writes
miss the second half's reads and writes, so a pair whose halves write one
register always takes those two paths, with the JIT on or off. A head that leaves a
register's value as it was can't be told from one that didn't write it;
then the second half's value stays. Crate test
`pair_head_wins_over_its_second_half`; fwtest's harness test of the same
name. fwtest's firmware suite gives the same outputs with and without it.
0012 since 0.7.0 (session spec-overnight-1025), written here from the
app's behaviour-only note, not its code: the two should behave the same

# Upstream note: a dual-issue pair whose halves write one register

For the owner to apply in the F-Emulator app, and to offer to
`joakimeriksson/fm1-emu` if wanted. Spec side only; not filed by a
session. Written in session day-1024 (2026-10-24) against commit
`43ed5580064885e93bc8d20be931ae950d10cd4f`; our copy carries the change as
`vendor/emulator/patches/0011-pair-head-wins-over-its-second-half.patch`
(fwtest 0.6.0). docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md lists it.

## What upstream does

`fm1-core` holds a pair head's register results until the second half has
run, then commits those the second half didn't change. When both halves
write the same register, the second half's value stays.

## What the vendor compiler expects

The head's. It pairs a head computing a value with a word load into the
same register whose result it doesn't use, then uses the register as the
head's value:

```
r7 = r6 + 0x80000  #
r7 = [r1+8]
r5 = r7 >> 16
```

(an unused read of SPI0's `BUF` in a flash routine at `-Os`; at `-O2` also
`r0 = r1.b0 (u) #` and `r0 = uextra(r1, p:8, l:8) #` with `r0 = [r3+8]`,
then `[r3+8] = r0`). In everything we compiled, these are the only pairs
whose halves write one register, and each uses the head's value next.

## What the patch does

Both commit loops (`step` and `exec_fast_paired`) commit every register
the head changed, over the second half's write. The JIT needs nothing: the
block builder glues a pair into compiled code only when the head's writes
miss the second half's reads and writes, so a pair whose halves write one
register always takes those two paths, with the JIT on or off. A head that leaves a
register's value as it was can't be told from one that didn't write it;
then the second half's value stays. Crate test
`pair_head_wins_over_its_second_half`; fwtest's harness test of the same
name. fwtest's firmware suite gives the same outputs with and without it.

app's behaviour-only note, not its code: the two should behave the same
(`fm1-emu-usb-port.md`), though the lines differ.

### SR-9: Flash storage: the region firmware may use, the part, and code while the flash is busy
- Asked: 2026-10-24, session M7 (firmware side)
- Question: (a) On an FM-1, which flash chip offsets our firmware may use
  for its own data without harming the boot chain or the update path:
  what lies below `0x4000`, whether anything past an installed image
  (the chip's last sectors, say) is used by the boot chain or the update
  path, and the chip's size on the FM-1. (b) The FM-1's flash part, and
  from its datasheet: the 4 KiB erase's and the page program's times
  (typical and maximum), the endurance (erase cycles a sector), and
  whether it can suspend an erase or program. (c) On the chip, while an
  erase or a program is in progress: what reads through the code window
  do (wait until it ends, read wrong data, fault), for core 1 too.
  busy times, the wrap and the write enable). Also: fwtest 0.5.0 runs a
  dual-issue pair whose two halves write one register differently from
  the compiler's expectation, which a flash driver can meet (HARNESS.md,
  "Instructions", the known gap). Open: Q-21 to Q-24.
- Answered: 2026-10-24, session day-1024 (spec side)
- **Q-26. What the chip's loaders and updater check.** What the mask ROM
  and `uboot.boot` check before running the next step (CRCs, the key
  block, the directory), whether the chip key is the same on every unit,
  and what the stock updater and the update loader `ota.bin` accept
  (HW-92; FM-1-RE has not found all of the updater's check). Settled only
  on a unit (Phase B; M9-PLAN.md section 5) or by JieLi's documentation.

`joakimeriksson/fm1-emu` if wanted. Spec side only; not filed by a
session. Written in session spec-1027 (2026-10-27) against commit
`43ed5580064885e93bc8d20be931ae950d10cd4f`; our copy carries the change as
`vendor/emulator/patches/0013-store-of-the-base-keeps-its-old-value.patch`
(fwtest 0.9.0). docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md lists it.

## What upstream does

A pre-increment store with a number step moves the base, then reads the
register to store, so `[++r4=748] = r4` stores the moved base. That holds
for the word, halfword and byte forms, on every path that runs them
(`Fast::StPre`, the syntax-driven store, routes 19 and 35). The
post-increment stores, and the pre-increment store with a register step
(route 32), read the register first and store the base as it was.

## What the vendor compiler expects

The base as it was. For

```
int *f(int *p) { int *q = p + 187; *q = (int)p; return q; }
```

it emits the one instruction `[++r0=748] = r0`, and `[r0++=8] = r0`,
`h[++r0=8] = r0` and `b[++r0=8] = r0` for the post-increment, halfword
and byte versions. For the same C storing the moved pointer (`*q = q`) it
computes the new base in another register and stores that. A firmware
built on small-beeps faulted on code compiled this way, depending only on
register allocation. What the chip stores has not been measured.

## What the patch does

Each store path reads the register to store before it moves the base.
Loads, and register-pair accesses whose base is in the pair, are
unchanged. The JIT has no pre-increment store of its own. Crate test
`stores_of_the_base_keep_its_old_value` (all fifteen forms the assembler
takes); fwtest's harness test of the same name.
""")

config: pin fwtest 0.7.0
**First in the merge order.** One commit.

**What:** `config/fwtest-image` moves to fwtest 0.7.0's digest (`sha256:d7804526…677e`), published from main when #137 merged.

**Why:** the owner's prompt for this session, section 1; R-SEP-3. 0.7.0 adds the USB core's register access port (docs/HARNESS.md, the versions' list; docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md, 0012), which our firmware doesn't use.

**How:** the digest comes from the push step of the image workflow's run on `d28ec99`. The firmware suite (the store's nine cases included) and the ARP suite ran on main's image (`7c41f08a…`), once on 0.6.0 and once on 0.7.0, and the output trees were compared file by file.

**Result:**
- Both suites PASS on both versions. `tests/test_store.py` OK.
- **No output changed.** 3 480 files were compared: the firmware suite's 3 089 and the ARP suite's 391. The 633 that differ hold only fwtest's version and the image digest (`result.json`, `runner.txt`), plus `runner.txt`'s status line where the 0.6.0 ARP run named its image with `FWTEST_IMAGE`.
